metrics.result:
I made the square Bean Box post as a 9-second, 1080×1080 MP4 at `./out/film.mp4`. The script is `./film.reel`. Lint is clean, and I checked one frame by eye. I didn't check the finished MP4 itself.

- **Look:** cream `#FFF4E6` background with three full-width orange `#FF6B35` pills reading "Fresh roasted", "Free shipping" and "Cancel anytime". Each pill pops in one after the other, then pulses.
- **Header:** "BEAN BOX" with a small orange bar under "Coffee subscription". The "Coffee subscription" line is my own wording, so change it if you'd rather not have it.
- **Text colour:** the title and pill text are dark brown, not orange or cream. Orange text on cream, and cream text on orange, both failed the contrast check (about 2.6:1, below the 3:1 minimum). The orange stays on the pills and the bar.
- **Ending:** the whole stack pulses once near the end, then holds still.

The bare `agentfx` command in this session couldn't find its renderer. I ran the built binary at `/home/drzivil/dev/agentfx/target/release/agentfx` instead.

checklist.evidence: Orange pills and bar on a cream background.
Fresh roasted, Free shipping and Cancel anytime are all visible and legible.
BEAN BOX is large at the top of every frame.

problems: The layout is top-heavy. The bottom ~15% of the frame is empty, and the empty space is uneven.
The three pills are identical, full-width orange blocks. There are no icons or imagery, and no coffee or bean visual, so the post feels generic.
The first ~1s shows only the title with an empty lower half, and the pills stack in slowly. The cards are all in by ~2.5s, followed by about 6s of near-static holding.
The dark text on saturated orange has only moderate contrast. Everything is the same weight, so no feature stands out.
There is no call to action or URL, such as 'Subscribe' or a website, and the tagline is small and plain.
judge.verdict: The post meets the brief. It is square, uses orange on cream, shows all three features and shows the Bean Box name, and the text is legible. It is a clean but generic template, with a top-heavy layout, no imagery and no call to action. A user would probably accept it as a first draft, though a designer wouldn't call it polished.
